headline: Russia's last independent paper closed Monday.
summary: Novaya Gazeta, started in 1993, cleared out its Moscow office Monday. The government had blocked its websites, seized its printing house, cut off reader donations and ordered it out of the building. Six of its journalists have been killed. Its editor says it will return one day. A new sign went up outside: 'Here lived Novaya Gazeta.'

cover_question.q: Why did they make it stop?

cover_answer: The government. It wrote things the government didn't like.
table_question: If you can't ban something, is making it impossible the same thing?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: In Russia, a newspaper that told people what the government was doing wrong had to stop. The government blocked its websites, took its printing machines and told it to leave its building. It's like being told you can't use the classroom anymore, so the class ends. It happened far away, and the grown-ups are watching it.
5-7.why: A paper told to stop, and a classroom taken away: the whole story at six. Putin and the war stay in the background.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script hands over one paper told to stop and a classroom taken away, which they have felt. Putin and Ukraine never come up. Expect 'can they write it at home?' Some reporters moved abroad in 2022 and started a new paper there. The editor says this one will come back.

8-12.script: Novaya Gazeta spent 33 years reporting on corruption in Russia. After Putin invaded Ukraine, the government blocked its websites, seized its printing house, cut off donations and ordered it out of its office. No step was a ban. Together they ended the paper. A referee calling a foul on every touch.
8-12.why: Steps that add up to a shutdown: a chain to follow and judge at eleven.
8-12.why_long: At eleven they work out rules and whether adults apply them, so the script runs one chain: websites blocked, printing house seized, donations cut off, office taken, paper gone. The referee calling a foul on every touch is the mechanism they know. Expect 'is that allowed?' In Russia now, yes. The paper says rights there are abolished.

13-17.script: Nobody banned Novaya Gazeta. The government blocked its sites, took its press, cut off its money and evicted it. Is that different from a ban, or just slower? Six of its journalists were killed and it kept going. Second: the editor says it will return once the country stirs. Do you believe him?
13-17.why: Never banned, and gone: both true. At sixteen they can hold both.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: no law ever banned Novaya Gazeta, and the paper is gone. The script asks whether a slow squeeze is a ban by another name, and they are testing whether you will argue it honestly. Expect 'why care about one paper?' It was the last one inside Russia still critical of the Kremlin.

5-7.q: Why did they make it stop?
5-7.a: The government. The paper wrote about things the government did wrong, and it didn't like that.

8-12.q: Why would a government shut a newspaper?
8-12.a: It exposed corruption. It says defending rights is now a crime there.

8-12.q: Can't they just put it online?
8-12.a: Its websites are blocked. Staff who left in 2022 run one from abroad.

13-17.q: Why not just keep printing anyway?
13-17.a: They tried four years. Sites blocked, press seized, license revoked.

13-17.q: Why didn't they all just leave Russia?
13-17.a: Some did, in 2022. The ones who stayed say the office was their home.
